To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) smartness is a property of a sociotechnical system, (ii) the system is composed of physical, informational, regulatory, and social layers, and (iii) smartness can be achieved only when these layers are considered together.

(1) smart appliances may be dumb in terms of system efficiency, because their aggregate effect can be counterproductive, and (2) this is the consequence of a reductionist approach that does not recognize the complexity of the sociotechnical system.

(1) a system composed of many independent, but interconnected, devices that are reacting to the same signal is likely to be less stable than a single device, and (2) a system composed only of interconnected devices is likely to be unstable, regardless of the number of devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to develop a more comprehensive and realistic model of the electrical system, which can then serve as the basis for the design of more effective demand?response policies.
the unintended consequences of the smartness of appliances, and we argue that a more holistic approach is required to design effective and stable demand? response policies.
the design of a new approach to the management of the power grid, and we argue that the current approach, which is based on the idealization of the system, is insufficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the smartness of the appliances is not enough for a smart grid, as the latter requires an appropriate design of the system as a whole.
the smartness of a system is the product of its components, which is not necessarily positive.
the smartness of individual appliances is not enough to ensure the smartness of a system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
smart appliances are not necessarily smart for the system as a whole.
the smartness of the system is the result of a complex interplay of the different layers, and it is the result of an emergent process.
, in order to improve the stability and efficiency of power grids, we should not only focus on the technological side but also on the regulatory and informational ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smart grid is not a simple matter of smart appliances, and the smart grid is more than a smart grid.
the design of a smart system should be done in a way that is mindful of the system?s complexity and that it is not enough to consider only a single aspect of it.
